summary: 仿生学从生物已经适应环境的结构和过程寻找工程办法。文章从魔术贴讲到模仿海洋生物的发电装置、受白蚁巢启发的建筑降温，以及人工模拟光合作用的尝试。

sentences: Velcro, now commonly used instead of buttons and zippers, is probably the most famous example of ‘biomimicry’, where technologists turn to nature for inspiration.
如今常代替纽扣和拉链的魔术贴，可能是最著名的仿生实例：技术人员向自然寻找灵感。
In 1948, scientist Georges de Mestral was walking through long grass when he noticed that dozens of seeds had attached themselves to his trousers.
1948年，科学家乔治·德梅斯特拉尔走过高草丛时，发现几十颗种子粘上了裤子。
Under a microscope, de Mestral noted the hook-and-loop system the seed cases used to stick so firmly, and was inspired.
透过显微镜，他看清种子外壳靠钩环结构牢牢附着，由此获得灵感。
paragraphs.gist: 科学家德梅斯特拉尔观察到草籽牢牢粘在裤子上，用显微镜看清钩环结构后从中获得启发，这便是魔术贴的仿生来源。

sentences: US biologist Janine Benyus wrote a book on the subject called Biomimicry: Innovation Inspired by Nature.
美国生物学家珍妮·贝纽斯为此写了《仿生学：自然启发的创新》一书。
Published in 1997, the book set off the current wave of technology modelled on nature.
这本书于1997年出版，掀起了当代仿生技术的热潮。
According to Benyus, our ancestors were practised in the art of biomimicry.
贝纽斯认为，我们的祖先本来就善于仿生。
‘I think it’s an old impulse for humans to take their cues from other organisms,’ she says, referring to African tribes that found edible plants by observing the dining habits of chimpanzees.
她说：“向其他生物学习，我想这是人类自古就有的冲动。”她举的例子是，非洲一些部族通过观察黑猩猩吃什么来辨认可食植物。
But lately we’ve become more focused on what we can make ourselves.
但最近我们更加关注自己能做些什么。

Benyus thinks our drift away from nature started with the advent of agriculture: ‘When we broke free from the challenges of hunting and gathering and learnt to stock our cupboards, we fooled ourselves into believing that we didn’t need other organisms at all,’ she says.
本纽斯认为，人类从农业出现后开始疏远自然。她说：“当我们摆脱狩猎采集的艰辛，学会把食橱装满时，就误以为自己完全不再需要其他生物了。”
paragraphs.gist: 贝纽斯的著作带动现代仿生热潮，但她认为人类早就向其他生物学习，农业兴起、食物能够储存后才逐渐忽略了这种依存。

paragraphs.brief: 资源约束重启向自然学习
sentences: The scientific, industrial, petrochemical and genetic engineering revolutions have repeatedly reinforced the idea that we are liberated from biological constraints.
科学、工业、石化和遗传工程革命一再强化了我们摆脱生物限制的理念。
In recent years, however, the illusion that we are independent of nature has been shattered by the spectre of global warming and the looming end to fossil fuel supplies.
然而，全球变暖的威胁与化石燃料供应可能枯竭的前景，已打破人类能独立于自然的幻想。

Since few of us would be willing to forgo the products and services we’ve grown accustomed to – food, water, shelter, the conveniences that modern technology brings – the challenge is to meet the complex demands of civilisation within the bounds of sustainability.
很少有人甘愿放弃食物、洁水、住所和技术便利等已习以为常的产品与服务，难题就在于如何可持续地满足文明的复杂需求。
‘Nature has learnt to fly, live in the depths of the ocean and craft miracle materials,’ writes Benyus.
贝纽斯写道：“自然界的生物学会了飞行、居住在海洋深处，还会制造神奇的材料。
‘Living creatures have done everything we want to do, without guzzling fossil fuel or polluting the planet.
它们已做成了我们想做的事，又不大量消耗化石燃料或污染地球。
What better models could there be?’
还有比这些更好的榜样吗？”
paragraphs.gist: 资源趋紧和全球变暖让人们重新思考对自然的依赖，而生物能以较少能源完成飞行、造材等任务，为可持续技术提供了范本。

paragraphs.brief: 反用鲨尾原理获取潮汐能
sentences: There are no better models, according to Tim Finnigan, a marine engineer at the University of Sydney.
悉尼大学海洋工程师蒂姆·芬尼根认为，没有更好的榜样了。
In his quest to harness the world’s waves and tides for renewable energy more efficiently, Finnigan has taken his cues from aquatic life.
为更高效地利用波浪和潮汐开发可再生能源，芬尼根向水生生物寻求灵感。
With their streamlined bodies and stiff, high tail fins, sharks convert up to 90 per cent of their body energy into forward thrust.
鲨鱼具有流线型身体和又高又挺的尾鳍，体内能量多达百分之九十可转为向前的推力。
Inspired by such efficient hydrodynamics, but turning the theory on its head, Finnigan designed his tidal stream generator: an 18-metre-long biomimetic shark tail with a fin spanning 15 metres.
受这种高效水动力结构启发，芬尼根把原理倒过来运用，设计出潮流发电机：仿生鲨尾长十八米，尾鳍张开宽十五米。
‘Rather than have a body moving through a stationary fluid, we have fluid that’s moving past a stationary body,’ says Finnigan.
芬尼根说：“不是让物体在静止的水中运动，而是让流动的水经过固定的物体。”
paragraphs.gist: 芬尼根借用鲨尾高效推进的原理，把运动关系倒转，让潮流经过固定的仿生尾鳍，设计出用于获取可再生能源的潮流发电机。

paragraphs.brief: 仿海藻随浪调整发电装置
sentences: Then there’s Finnigan’s biomimetic forest of giant seaweed.
芬尼根还设计了一片仿巨型海藻林的装置。
‘As a diver I’ve looked at the way motions occur under water in the presence of waves,’ he says.
他说：“我潜水时留意过有波浪时水下的运动。
‘I see plants that move quite dramatically and yet they never seem to be pulled out, even in the most dramatic waves.’
我看见水生植物大幅摆动，可就算风浪很大，它们似乎也不会被连根拔起。”
The trouble with conventional designs, according to Finnigan, is that they’re made to stand rigidly against the power of the ocean.
芬尼根认为，传统设计的问题在于硬顶海洋的力量。
‘The structures we try to build in the ocean just never end up being strong enough to survive out there,’ says Finnigan.
他说：“我们试着建在海里的结构，到头来总是不够结实，撑不住那里的条件。”
In the manner of aquatic plants and animals, Finnigan’s designs respond to changing current or wave conditions by reorienting to maximise energy capture.
他的设计像水生动植物一样，随海流和波浪的变化调整方向，以获得最多能量。
And in severe weather, to avoid a battering, his wave energy generator will lie flat against the ocean floor.
恶劣天气下，波浪发电装置会平伏在海床上，以免遭受冲击。
paragraphs.gist: 观察海藻随浪弯曲却不易被拔起后，芬尼根让发电装置能转向获取更多能量，在恶劣天气又可贴伏海床避开冲击。

paragraphs.brief: 从白蚁丘借鉴办公楼降温
sentences: While conventional architects were designing buildings dependent on expensive air conditioning systems, when Mick Pearce tried to do the same, he struck a problem.
常规建筑设计依赖昂贵的空调系统；米克·皮尔斯本也想照此设计，却遇到了难题。
‘We were building office blocks for a client in Zimbabwe and we ran out of funds.
“我们在为津巴布韦的一位客户建办公楼时，经费用光了。
So we looked for ways to make a building without traditional air conditioning.’
于是我们就寻找不用传统空调也能建楼的办法。”
One day, driving through the grasslands, he saw a large mound created by termites, the ant-like insect common in Africa.
一天，他驾车穿过草原时，看见一座巨大的白蚁丘；白蚁是一种在非洲常见、外形像蚂蚁的昆虫。
He noticed that air entering at the base of the mound was mixed with water drawn from subterranean levels by the termites, causing evaporative cooling.
他发现，从丘底进入的空气与白蚁从地下带上来的水接触，水分蒸发带走了热量。

Pearce wanted to reproduce this principle but he needed an alternative system, and in his building massive fans were employed at the base of the structure to lower the temperature of the circulating air.
皮尔斯想借用这一原理，但需要另一套实现方式，于是在建筑底部安装大型风机，降低循环空气的温度。
Pearce’s termite-inspired cooling system cut energy use to 10 per cent of a similar air-conditioned building.
这套受白蚁启发的降温系统，耗能仅为配有空调的同类建筑的十分之一。
paragraphs.gist: 皮尔斯为节省津巴布韦写字楼的空调费用，从白蚁丘的通风降温方式获得启发，最终把能耗降到类似空调建筑的十分之一。

paragraphs.brief: 实验室可调控光合作用条件
sentences: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use energy from the sun to convert water and carbon dioxide into carbohydrates and oxygen.
光合作用是绿色植物利用太阳能量将水和二氧化碳转化为碳水化合物和氧的过程。
Plants can manage it with humbling ease.
植物能举重若轻地完成这个过程，令人自叹不如。
But, as the 40 researchers from 11 institutes who have collaborated to form the Australian Artificial Photosynthesis Network have realised, it is very complex.
然而，来自十一个机构、合作组成澳大利亚人工光合作用网络的四十名研究者发现，这个过程极其复杂。
However, there is one aspect working in our favour.
然而，有一个方面有利于我们。
In nature, environmental variables like temperature, carbon dioxide and light availability limit the rate of photosynthesis.
在自然界，温度、二氧化碳和光线供应等环境变量限制了光合作用率。
In a laboratory these variables can be optimized.
在实验室中，这些变量是可以优化的。
‘We don’t have to cope with drought or frost.
“我们不必应付干旱和霜冻。
We can work with a highly controlled, specified set of conditions,’ says Tom Collings, the group’s spokesman.
可以在一组明确、可高度控制的条件下工作，”该团队发言人汤姆·科林斯说。
paragraphs.gist: 人工复制光合作用极其复杂，但实验室可以精细控制温度、光照和二氧化碳，也无须应对霜冻干旱，这是天然环境没有的优势。

items.en: a reference to a natural process that appears simpler than it actually is
items.zh: 一种实际比看上去更复杂的自然过程。
items.why: 先说光合作用看似容易，紧接着指出其实“very complex",符合“看似简单却并不简单的自然过程”。

items.en: a description of an invention that can protect itself under extreme conditions
items.zh: 描述可以在极端条件下自我保护的发明
items.why: 这款仿巨藻的发电装置在极端海况下可“躺平" 自保，正是“能在恶劣条件下自我保护的发明”。

items.en: the reasons why humans no longer feel they are free from nature
items.zh: 人们为何不再认为自己可以摆脱自然的制约。
items.why: 文中指出，气候变暖和化石燃料枯竭令人类意识到，自己仍然受自然条件制约。

items.en: a reference to an animal that influenced the diet of some humans
items.zh: 一种动物如何影响了一些人的饮食。
items.why: 非洲一些部族通过观察黑猩猩觅食辨认出可食用的植物，这是动物影响人类饮食的例子。

items.en: specific reasons why science should copy nature
items.zh: 科学研究应当向自然借鉴的具体理由。
items.why: 自然已经发展出飞行、深海生存及制造特殊材料的能力，作者用这些实例解释科学为何可向自然借鉴。

items.en: Designs often fail when they try to resist natural forces.
items.zh: 设计在试图抵抗自然力量时往往失败。

items.en: Science has certain key advantages over nature.
items.zh: 科学比自然具有某些关键优势。

items.en: People have been copying nature for thousands of years.
items.zh: 人们模仿自然已有数千年。

items.en: A shortage of money can inspire innovative design.
items.zh: 资金短缺可以激发创新设计。

items.en: The discovery that humans could produce food themselves caused them to turn away from nature.
items.zh: 人类发现可以自行生产食物之后，便开始疏远自然。

items.en: The design of his office block can be compared to that of a termite’s ________.
items.zh: 他设计的办公楼，其构造可以与白蚁的________相类比。
items.why: Pearce 的写字楼比作白蚁的“mound”。

items.en: Termites use ________ to cool the air, but in Pearce’s system this cooling effect was produced by ____ (Q26).
items.zh: 白蚁借助________给空气降温，皮尔斯的系统则靠________（Q26）达到同样的降温效果。
items.why: 白蚁利用水进行蒸发冷却。

items.en: Termites use ____ (Q25) to cool the air, but in Pearce’s system this cooling effect was produced by ________.
items.zh: 白蚁借助________（Q25）给空气降温，皮尔斯的系统则靠________达到同样的降温效果。
items.why: Pearce 用风扇取代白蚁的水来产生冷却效果。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

pairs: 例子把极端条件具体化为会冲击发电设备的恶劣天气。
两处都在谈人能否摆脱对自然的依赖。原文把这种独立视为已经破灭的幻觉。
stand rigidly against the power of the ocean
题干用“抵抗自然力”概括原文所描写的设计，即用刚性结构硬抗海浪。
points: 自然已经发展出飞行、深海生存及制造特殊材料的能力，作者用这些实例解释科学为何可向自然借鉴。
Pearce 的写字楼比作白蚁的“mound”。
clauses: Velcro, now commonly used instead of buttons and zippers, is probably the most famous example of ‘biomimicry’, ….
“where technologists turn to nature for inspiration”修饰前面的 example。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 where 时，回看 example，再把修饰信息接回主句。
In 1948, scientist Georges de Mestral was walking through long grass when he noticed ….
“that dozens of seeds had attached themselves to his trousers”补足 noticed 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 noticed 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
